tossups.text: It generalizes to the principle of corresponding states, and approximates a virial term as half the square of the number of particles, so it is only valid for very large numbers of particles. Derived by its namesake in 1881, one of its fit parameters accounts for the magnitude of its namesake's intermolecular forces. For 10 points, identify the equation of state that corrects the ideal gas law's assumption of point-like, non-interacting particles with two parameters, often called a and b.

Virchow's triad must be satisfied for these objects to form. Mutations in factors V [five] through XI [eleven] lead to their overproduction. tPA [T-P-A] is administered to break down these structures, which require tissue factor to form. They are composed of fibrin. Heparin and warfarin, which block the activity of Vitamin K, are administered to prevent formation of these objects. One of these structures forms in an ischemic stroke, blocking blood supply to the brain. These structures won't form in hemophiliacs. For 10 points, name these objects that form in thromboembolisms, when platelets aggregate, to stop bleeding.

The fallout from this event caused a participant to have a mental breakdown, quit his job, and become Vice President of Polaroid. The "Kranz Dictum" was surmised in the aftermath of this event, which was most prominently covered in the media by Jules Bergman. A board review of this event, whose participants mistrusted Joseph Shea, focused on the danger of materials like 34 square feet of velcro. The circumstances of this event mirrored an event six years earlier surrounding Valentin Bondarenko, whose death was suppressed until 1980. During a Senate Committee hearing about this event, Walter Mondale publicized the Phillips Report. This event occurred during a "plugs-out test" with Ed White, Roger Chaffee, and Gus Grissom. For 10 points, name this 1967 disaster that occurred during a preflight launch rehearsal at Cape Canaveral.
acceptableAnswers: accept destruction of the Apollo 1 modules
the deaths of the Apollo 1 astronauts

tossups.text: Ruth Barcan Marcus argued that a consistent set of these things could only exist if there was a possible world where the entire set was obeyable. R.M. Hare argued that these things possess universalizability and prescriptivity in a book titled for the Language of these things. A paper titled for these things argues that secular approaches to them lack grounding and coined the term "consequentialism." That paper by G.E.M. Anscombe is titled for the modern philosophy of these things. Bernard Williams introduced a situation that results when agents are assigned blame for things that they had no control over, which he termed these things' "luck." For 10 points, name these things, the guiding principles for determining right and wrong.

The narrator of a novel set during this event hears Juliek playing Beethoven on the violin the night before he dies. This event's perpetrators are depicted as cats in Art Spiegelman's graphic novel Maus. Miep Gies ["Meep Geese"] recovered a work written during this event, which is largely addressed to "Kitty." In a trilogy beginning with Night, Elie Wiesel ["eh-lye vie-zehl"] wrote about experiencing this event. The Diary of a Young Girl was written by a victim of this event, Anne Frank. For 10 points, memoirs about what Nazi-led event often detail Jewish authors' experiences in concentration camps?

Norman Bailey posited that a conflict in this country was driven by either sexual frustration or a principle translated as "not even leaving the seed." "Peasant leagues" in this country were organized by the PCC to counter government violence. Jacobo Arenas wrote a diary about his organizing of the peasant-controlled "Marquetalia Republic" in this country. The Benidorm Pact preceded the Sitges Pact that ended a conflict in this country by establishing the National Front coalition. Reactions to the "Regeneration" movement sparked the Thousand Days' War in this country. Mariano Ospina Perez led this country at the start of a period during which Gustavo Rojas Pinilla rose to power. Juan Roa's murder of Liberal Party candidate Jorge Eliecer Gaitan led to a bloody ten-year civil war in this country. For 10 points, name this country, the site of La Violencia.

This thinker defined property in terms of work done on natural substances in a work that was partly written in response to Robert Filmer. He divided properties of objects into primary and secondary qualities. He claimed that, because man leaves the state of nature to gain the protection of government, monarchs who do not protect their citizens can be overthrown. For 10 points, name this British empiricist who wrote Two Treatises on Government and the Essay Concerning Human Understanding, which proposed a mental blank slate called the "tabula rasa."

Bachi are used with a Japanese type of these instruments called taiko. An hourglass-shaped type of these instruments from West Africa is played while wedged between the arm and body and is called their "talking" type. A pitched type of these instruments common in Caribbean music is their "steel" type. Their "kettle" type includes the timpani. For 10 points, name these percussion instruments typically played with sticks.

One character in this novel has an epiphany when he fnds the "Bibliography of Bibliographies" that shows him all libraries are arranged in an organized taxonomy. One character in this novel refuses to have a child with her husband Walter because she does not want to pass on his mediocrity and becomes obsessed with the "musicality" of a murderer imprisoned for killing a 3 prostitute. The nymphomaniac Bonadea seduces the protagonist in this novel's frst volume, "A Sort of Introduction," which begins when the main character decides to take a "vacation from life." The main character meets his twin sister Agathe in this novel's last volume, titled "Into the Millennium: The Criminals," and watches as his neighbor Clarisse becomes fxated on the imprisoned murderer Moosburger. Count Leinsdorf leads the "Collateral Campaign" in this novel that is planning a massive celebration for the 70th anniversary of the reign of Franz Joseph I. Set in the fctional country of Kakania, for 10 points, name this unfnished novel about the aimless Ulrich in fn-de-si`ecle Vienna, written by Robert Musil.

After reading The Count of Monte Cristo, a character in this novel fantasizes about saying "Madam, I never eat muscatel grapes" to Mercedes. This novel ends with its protagonist resolving to "forge in the smithy of my soul the uncreated conscience of my race." The main character of this novel feels an angel has appeared to him after making eye contact with a girl wading in the sea. This novel's protagonist is almost punished for breaking his glasses while attending Clongowes school, a place he is later reminded of while listening to a fiery sermon about hell at a Jesuit retreat. This novel opens with a stream of consciousness rendition of a children's story about baby tuckoo and a moocow. For 10 points, name this novel about Stephen Dedalus's intellectual development by James Joyce.
tossups.answer: Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
acceptableAnswers: Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
The Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

tossups.text: In human physiology, this structure is essential for hypothalamic hormones. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hypothalamus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hypothalamus is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in hypothalamic hormones.

tossups.text: Although the Supreme Court found in favor of this case's plaintiff regarding a dispute over a commission, it refused to issue a writ of mandamus because it also found that the law that had allowed it to hear this case was unconstitutional. In this case, the Judiciary Act of 1789 became the first law to be struck down by the Supreme Court. For 10 points, identify this 1803 court case which established the principle of judicial review.

Henry Briggs published a table of values resulting from this non-trigonometric operation. A slide rule uses the properties of this operation to make efficient calculations. This operation, which was discovered by John Napier, can be used to find the number of digits in a given number. The "common" kind of this operation has a base of ten, while its "natural" kind, often abbreviated "ln" ["L-N"], has a base equal to Euler's number, e. For 10 points, name this operation, which is the inverse of exponentiation.
acceptableAnswers: accept log base e and log base ten
accept ln before it is read

tossups.text: The Thirty Tyrants were installed in this city after its defeat in the Peloponnesian War. A 429 BCE plague killed a leader of this city who ushered in a golden age and transformed the Delian League into an empire. Pericles was a leader of this city, which was also led by a man known for his harsh laws, Draco. In this city, the Parthenon was constructed to honor its namesake goddess of wisdom. For 10 points, name this birthplace of democracy, a Greek city-state that rivaled Sparta.

In this epic, Eurycleia [yoo-ree-CLAY-ah] discovers the secret identity of a beggar, but is prevented from telling her employer by Athena. The dog Argos dies after seeing his master in this epic, in which a "cunning man" uses the herb "moly" to trick Circe. This epic's title character lives with Calypso for seven years, and shoots an arrow through twelve axes to reclaim his place with Penelope and Telemachus in Ithaca. For 10 points, name this epic poem attributed to Homer about the title hero's long journey home from the Trojan War.

An album beginning with this word references a rock scene that was first named on Urge Overkill's EP Stull. Guitarist Casey Rice was recruited to play the opening riff of an album with a title beginning with this word, which opens with the lines "I bet you fall in bed too easily / With the beautiful girls who are shyly brave." A debut album whose title begins with this word had its origins in the demo cassettes recorded by its songwriter under the name Girly Sound while an art student at Oberlin; those demos include one for the song "Fuck and Run." A photo booth session at Chicago's Rainbow Club is the origin of the cover photo of an album beginning with this word that shows its artist with an open mouth and her eyes hidden by a purple hood. A 1993 alt-rock album whose title begins with this word contains the songs "Never Said" and "6'1''," and was written as a feminist response to a 1972 double album featuring "Tumbling Dice." Those two albums that each begin with this word are by Liz Phair and The Rolling Stones. For 10 points, what word proceeds "in Guyville" and "on Main St" in the titles of two iconic rock albums?

1. He wrote that the gold standard protects "from confiscation through inflation" in a paper entitled "Gold and Economic Freedom" that appeared in Ayn Rand's Capitalism: the Unknown Ideal. Succeeding Paul Volcker in his most famous post, his speeches on "irrational exuberance" caused drops in stock prices, though his statement that liquidity will be provided eased the severity of a 1987 stock market crash. Criticized by some who claim that he may have caused the recent recession with his loose monetary policies, for 10 points, identify this American economist who was succeeded by Ben Bernanke as Chairman of the Federal Reserve.

The Ackermann function must be expressed using this concept, and it is often used to define fractals such as the Sierpinski triangle. This technique is employed by the fastest algorithms for computing factorials, and its "tail-" form can emulate iterative processes. The operation of an algorithm of this kind continues until encountering a base case. For 10 points, name this technique from computer science employed by functions which call themselves.

In this city, riots broke out at Columbia Heights after the assassination of Martin Luther King. Pierre Charles L'Enfant created a plan for this city, which called for the construction of a building on Jenkins Hill. This city contains the world's largest obelisk, and State of the Unions are held within this city's Capitol Building. For 10 points name this city which contains the Lincoln Memorial and the White House, the capital of the United States.

this structure is essential for nail anatomy. It plays a key role in the integumentary system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hair follicle-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hair follicle is a key component of the Integumentary system, involved in nail anatomy.

parts.text: Name these non-metallic inorganic compounds. The oldest examples of this kind of material were made by firing clay in a kiln.

Ceramics that are vitrified to decrease permeability to water become one of these non-crystalline amorphous solids. A variety of it for laboratory use made from silica and boron trioxide is sold as Pyrex.
Boron trioxide is used to make Pyrex to lower its coefficient of this process, which increases the volume of a material in response to an increase in temperature.

parts.text: Name these plant hormones that mediate phototropism and gravitropism by causing cell growth and elongation. One example of these hormones is indole acetic acid.
These N6-adenine derivative plant hormones are primarily produced in root tips, with the most abundant kind being zeatin. Their main purpose is to regulate cell division.

Another class of plant hormones, gibberellins, encourage these structures to leave dormancy and germinate, allowing new plants to grow from them. These structures, consisting of an embryo, cotyledons, and their namesake coat, are found in fruits.

bonuses.leadin: PIN proteins transport the anionic form of these hormones across cell membranes. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this region. Conrad the Salic made Humbert the Whitehanded the first count of this region after he crushed an uprising in Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne ("sen-zhahn-duh-mor-YEN").
Amadeus VIII ("the eighth") conquered this city, which became the Savoyard capital. Amadeus's son, Louis, was gifted the ostensible burial shroud of Jesus, which is named for this city.

Savoyard influence in England began after this English king married Eleanor of Provence, who brought many relatives with her. This son of King John confirmed the Magna Carta and was the target of the Second Barons' War.

parts.text: Name these articles of faith revealed by God, which are binding upon faithful Catholics. No statement from the Second Vatican Council has this designation.

This document, also known as the Dogmatic Constitution of the Church, was approved at Vatican II by an overwhelming majority of bishops. This document declares in its second chapter that the Church is "the People of God."
This figure is given the title "Mediatrix" by Lumen Gentium. Pius XII defined dogma regarding this figure ex cathedra in the apostolic constitution, Munificentissimus Deus.

bonuses.leadin: This religious term is often used as a general name for unquestioningly accepted principles. For 10 points each:

Willa Cather set two of her Prairie novels in this western US state, where she grew up. Cather attended the state university in this state's capital, Lincoln.

parts.text: Name this Polish journalist who wrote books including Another Day of Life and The Emperor about conflicts he witnessed in Africa.
In The Emperor, Kapuscinski chronicled the palace intrigues and incompetent administration that led to the fall of this last emperor of Ethiopia at the hands of the military Derg government.

In Another Day of Life, Kapuscinski recounts several near-death experiences sustained while covering the beginning stages of this conflict, in which the MPLA was supported by a Cuban intervention against the South African-backed UNITA and Holden Roberto's FNLA.

parts.text: Name this gigantic choir that was founded in 1848 at the Latter-Day Saints temple in Salt Lake City.

All members of the Mormon Tabernacle Choir must be Mormons in good standings, which means all adult male singers have been granted the Melchizedek or Aaronic classes of this title. This religious position entitles men to act in the name of God to ensure their family's salvation.

Married members of the choir may have entered into this special type of marriage covenant that seals a man and woman together for eternity. Before undergoing this kind of marriage, one must get a recommendation from their temple and undergo an Endowment ceremony.
acceptableAnswers: new and everlasting covenant of marriage

Peter and the Wolf was written by this Russian composer. He also composed The Love for Three Oranges.
In Peter and the Wolf, the wolf is represented by this brass instrument, often played with one hand gripping the bell.

This bisexual Indian author of the poetry collections Mappings and All You Who Sleep Tonight wrote A Suitable Boy as well as the verse novel The Golden Gate.

parts.text: Name this event during which troops revolted in favor of Grand Duke Konstantin taking the Russian throne, despite him renouncing his claim. This revolt is known by a name taken from the month in which it occurred.
The Decembrist revolt was put down by a Russian ruler with this name, who later led Russia during its disastrous Crimean War. The second Russian ruler with this name was the last tsar of Russia.
About a hundred years later, another Russian revolt took place named after this other month. Sean Connery starred in a movie titled "The Hunt for Red [this month]" about a fictional Soviet submarine.

bonuses.leadin: This event took place after Alexander I's sudden death left the line of succession unclear. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this type of number that cannot be written as a terminating or repeating decimal number.

In the 18th century, Johann Lambert proved that pi is an irrational number by comparing a continuing fraction to this trigonometric function. Like the sine function, this trig function has the value zero when its input is zero.

A century later, Ferdinand Lindemann proved that pi is also this type of number, meaning that it cannot be the root of a non-zero polynomial equation with integer coefficients. Each real number is either one of these numbers, or an algebraic number.

bonuses.leadin: The Pythagoreans discovered that, because the diagonal of a square cannot be a multiple of the side of the square, the square root of 2 is this type of number. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this successor to Abraham Lincoln, who had eleven articles of impeachment brought against him after violating the Tenure of Office Act.
Johnson violated the Tenure of Office Act in trying to remove this man, his Secretary of War. This man also served as Buchanan's Attorney General.
Johnson frequently clashed with this group of politicians led by Thaddeus Stevens and Charles Sumner. This group denounced Lincoln's Reconstruction plans as too lenient.

parts.text: Name this creature of which a "surgeon's photograph" was taken in 1934 that has since been mostly debunked as a hoax. This large and long-necked creature supposedly inhabits a body of water in the Scottish Highlands.

Like the Loch (lock) Ness Monster, this creature is a cryptid, since its existence is unsubstantiated. This creature is described as a hairy and ape-like humanoid creature in North American forests which leaves giant footprints.

Sightings of this cryptid whose name means "goat-sucker" have mostly been in northern Mexico. This spiny creature supposedly the size of a large dog is said to attack and suck the blood from livestock.

Durkheim's most famous sociological study dealt with this phenomenon, the intentional ending of one's own life. Durkheim's study showed that, among other comparisons, soldiers performed it more often than civilians.
Durkheim described one cause of suicide by this French term, which describes a state in which individuals feel a lack of social structure and guidance.
